pr_title: Fix four issues for the WDAC logging feature
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary

Fix #20785 
Fix #20768

Address 4 issues for the WDAC logging feature:
- Hashtable-to-object conversion checking was wrong;
- A call to `GetPowerShell` and a call to `GetSteppablePipeline` show different behaviors when it's truly in Constrained mode, but the Audit feature didn't cover them.
- For the property/method access check in binder, fix the target name to also capture the target when `targetValue` is not a `Type` object.

### Steps to reproduce

Previously, in 7.3.9, I could use the Get-AzADGroup cmdlet from az.resources. This now fails in 7.4.0, logging the following warning to the event log, apparently due to Constrained Language mode. I have read the notes at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/scripting/learn/application-control?view=powershell-7.4#wdac-policy-enforcement but my understanding is that this is in warning-only mode, so not sure why this breaks.

Confirm 7.4.0 works fine where WDAC doesn't get involved. In both cases, $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode reads as "FullLanguage" but with WDAC, we get the below error.

Can also confirm that rolling back to 7.3.9, Get-AZADGroup works fine again.

### Expected behavior

PS > get-azadgroup -displayname azurevirtualdesktop

review_comments: I'm not sure about this - we're changing behavior with audit mode being enabled. Could you add a comment about why this is the right thing to do? If we're in CLM and because we're auditing now it's full language?

The Audit mode enables `ConstrainedLangaugeMode`, but it only logs the behavior difference resulted by this `ConstrainedLanguageMode` setting, without actually enforcing them. So, from the user's perspective, the script still runs in `FullLanguageMode`.

So here, if `context.LanguageMode == PSLanguageMode.ConstrainedLanguage` and we are in Audit, then we don't enforce the `ConstrainedLanguageMode`, but instead, assuming it's in `FullLanauge`. So, the user's script runs as if it's in the `FullLanguageMode`, but they receive events about what will/may not work in the real `ConstrainedLanguage`.

> we're changing behavior with audit mode being enabled.

Put it in another way, when in `Audit` mode, the script should behavior as if they are running in `FullLanguage` mode. We are not changing that behavior, but just logging what will/may fail in the real `ConstrainedLanguage` mode.
I didn't understand that audit mode implies constrained language mode - do you think a comment explaining this should be placed here (or above)?
A description about this should be put in the documentation of this Audit feature. I will check the documentation.

It's already in the documentation at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/scripting/learn/application-control?view=powershell-7.4#wdac-policy-auditing:
> In audit mode, PowerShell runs the untrusted scripts in **Constrained Language** mode without errors, but logs messages to the event log instead. The log messages describe what restrictions would apply if the policy was in Enforce mode.

this works, but reads a bit confusing since audit doesn't result in `canProceedWithConversion` but then does.  It may be less confusing for future readers to simply have the audit message written outside of this check and have this check include audit.
Made a bit refactoring and add a comment to make it clearer.

is there also a problem with the if/else in (now) 4010/4019. I thought that the audit mode was to _not_ change the behavior, and just log. However, if audit mode is enabled, then the exception 4021 will _not_ be thrown. It seemed to me that the `else` was an oversight and the throw should occur whether we're auditing or not.

The Audit mode enables `ConstrainedLangaugeMode`, but it only logs the behavior difference resulted by this `ConstrainedLanguageMode` setting, without actually enforcing them. So, from the user's perspective, the script still runs in `FullLanguageMode`.

The exception originally at line 4021 will be thrown only if it is NOT running in `FullLanguageModule`, or it's in the transition from `ConstrainedLanguageMode` to `FullLanguageMode`. Both checks don't matter when it's in Audit mode, we should just log what would really happen in `ConstrainedLanguageMode`, but still allow the conversion to proceed.
